title: Mayer--Vietoris gluing in ambient source-open coordinates
statement: Let X'→X, S'→S be a cartesian square, with S,S' affine and f:X→S quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-pc-scheme]. Let K,K' have quasi-coherent derived cohomology and φ:L(g')*K→K' [def-pc-derived-category]. For opens U,V of X with U,V,U∩V quasi-compact, if the explicit comparisons b_U,b_V,b_(U∩V) [def-pc-single-complex-open-comparison] are isomorphisms, then b_(U∪V) is an isomorphism. U and V need not cover X. There is no stalk-condition hypothesis in this gluing statement.

source.place: Tag 0DJ9 (lemma-single-complex-base-change), induction step, applied to the source U union V

proof.text: Set W=U∪V and form the cartesian square by pasting the defining pullback of g′ along W→X with the given square. Compactness of W follows from IsCompact.union. Over affine S, quasi-separated f makes X quasi-separated; a compact source W gives quasi-compact W→X and hence qcqs W→S. Inside W put A=(W→X)⁻¹U and B=(W→X)⁻¹V. Inverse image preserves intersections and unions, so A∪B=W. Quasi-compact W→X and the three compactness hypotheses give compact A, B and A∩B. These geometric checks are direct applications of Mathlib instances and its inverse-image lemmas.

Restrict K along W→X and K′ along the projection X′×_X W→X′; the derived pullback preservation theorem supplies quasi-coherent cohomology. Construct the restricted coefficient arrow explicitly by the same pullback-composition expression in singleComplexOpenComparison.

Apply the nested-comparison invariance theorem to U⊆W, V⊆W and U∩V⊆W. Its forward direction transports the three given ambient isomorphisms to the three hypotheses of relative Mayer–Vietoris on A, B and A∩B.

Apply relativeMayerVietoris to the restricted square and cover A∪B=W. Its conclusion is definitionally the ambient singleComplexOpenComparison on W: the definition uses exactly this square, these restricted complexes and this coefficient arrow. Proof irrelevance identifies the commutativity witnesses. Thus the required isomorphism follows.
